numbering_policy: Original Saints references, chapters, sections, anchors and continuation paragraphs are preserved. No mapping to another canon or Hebrew Psalm numbering.
review_notes: All 48 source verse units in Matthew 1–2 were read. Original source wording was not edited.
Genesis and Exodus target passages were re-read from the exact pinned files supplied in this update's work/cache-exact directory, after the parent identified differences in the older cache bytes.
Matthew 1:7–8 retains Asaph where the compared Chronicles genealogy has Asa, and Matthew 1:10 retains Amos where Chronicles has Amon. The rationales expose those differences.
The Saints reference for the Bethlehem ruler is Micah 5:1; the Rachel lament is Jeremiah 38:15; the royal-gift Psalm is Psalms 71. Another edition's numbers were not substituted.
Hosea 11:1 has 'summoned his children' in the pinned Saints English record; Matthew 2:15 has 'called My Son.' The quotation is retained with the wording difference and typological application stated.
Same-book and same-chapter links are explicitly described as internal literary or narrative links. They are not independent historical corroboration.
Matthew 2:23 is linked to actual Nazareth identifications in Luke and John. No unattested direct Old Testament Nazarene quotation or netser wordplay is asserted.

The comparison of Matthew's genealogical summary with Chronicles does not certify the three fourteen-generation counts, harmonize omitted generations, or resolve the Jacob/Heli and Jechoniah/Neri differences.
Read all 42 source units in Matthew chapters 3 and 4 in the saved Saints text. No source wording changes were proposed.
Retained targets were read directly in the Saints reference cache. Quotation wording differences were stated rather than silently harmonized.
Preserved Greek-based target numbering: Psalms 90:11–12; Isaiah 8:23 and 9:1. Isaiah 8:23–9:1 is one ordered cross-chapter target passage for the fulfillment introduction at Matthew 4:14.
The temptation sequence differs between Matthew and Luke. Angelic ministry in Mark's compressed account is not assigned Matthew's exact temporal placement.

Matthew 3:14 to John 1:26–27, Matthew 4:19 to Luke 5:10, and the regional crowd/healing comparisons are thematic parallels with their limitations stated; they do not claim an identical recorded exchange or occasion.
Matthew 3:15 remains deferred with zero completion credit. The Matthew 21:32 and 5:17 candidates were read but rejected for this batch as insufficiently specific.
All 111 source verse units in Matthew 5–7 were read from the supplied Saints English records. Source wording is unchanged; this file contains editorial proposals only.
Target passages were read from the supplied reference records; Exodus quotation targets were checked again against cache-exact/exodus.json after the parent identified an older cache copy.

Greek-based Saints numbering is retained: Exodus 20:15 is the murder command, Exodus 20:13 the adultery command, Psalm 36:11 the meek inheritance promise, Psalm 47:3 the city of the great King, and Psalm 6:9 the departure of lawless workers.

Parallels between Matthew and Luke preserve substantive differences, including poor in spirit versus poor; perfection versus mercy; the different petitions in the supplied Lord's Prayer texts; and different examples of parental gifts.
Leviticus 19:18 supports the love-your-neighbor clause in Matthew 5:43 and does not support the accompanying hate-your-enemy clause.
The Matthew 6:18 to 6:4 link is explicitly a same-chapter repeated formula. Other Matthew targets are in separate chapters.
Review is AI-assisted English passage comparison, not an exhaustive concordance, a fresh Greek critical-text review, or independent specialist approval.
interpretation_scope: Connections are labelled per pair; thematic parallels and allusions do not establish identical events, people or exact quotations.
source_limitations: NA28 is the user-authorized provisional New Testament base. Focused checks of the German Bible Society’s Greek running text are recorded by chapter. This is an English editorial revision, not complete critical-text or apparatus verification. The newer Bespoke PDF’s preferred UBS6 text has not been obtained; UBS6/ECM comparison, full apparatus, independent Greek and human read-aloud reviews remain pending.
